fields.meta_description: Build a roofing quote form that collects roof photos, emails your on-call lead about active leaks, and saves every request. Free to start.
fields.h1: Build a Roofing Quote Form Your Estimator Can Plan From
fields.hero_description: Build a roofing quote form that collects the roof's age, material, and photos, and keeps each request in a database you own.
fields.features_heading: Roof Requests That Arrive Ready to Inspect
fields.features_subheading: Emergent builds the roofing quote form, the table every request lands in, and the quote homeowners sign, from one prompt.
fields.feature_1:
Questions that follow the job type

Pick a leak repair and the form asks for the room below the leak and whether water is coming in now. Pick storm damage and it asks for the storm date and any insurance claim number.
fields.feature_2:
Roof photos from the homeowner's phone

Homeowners add photos of the roof and any ceiling stain as they fill in the form. Each photo stays with its request, and the estimator sees the damage before climbing a ladder.
fields.feature_3:
An email the moment water comes in

A yes to the leaking now question emails the on-call crew lead with the address and the photos. Name a backup, and the alert moves to them if nobody marks it handled in 15 minutes.
fields.feature_4:
No roof price before the inspection

Roof work shows no price on the form and goes to the estimator's list instead. Add-ons with a fixed rate, such as gutters by the foot, can show a price before the homeowner submits.
fields.feature_5:
Quotes signed on a phone

After the inspection, the estimator adds each option and its price to the quote. The homeowner picks one and signs on screen, and the status in the database changes to Signed.
fields.feature_6:
Your form's code in GitHub

On paid plans, export the code behind the quote form and its request table to your GitHub repository. Run it on your own servers, or give it to a developer who keeps building on it.

fields.usecase_heading: The Job Decides What the Form Asks
fields.tab_content_1:
With a yes to leaking now, Svea gets 2 photos

Anton Dobrev finds a brown stain spreading across his kitchen ceiling at 9:40 p.m. On Slatewood Roofing's form he picks a leak repair, answers yes to water coming in now, and adds 2 photos. Svea, the on-call crew lead, gets an email with his address and both photos. The request shows no price.
fields.tab_content_2:
On Severin's storm list, the soonest adjuster visit is first

Hail hit Gus Vinterberg's street on October 18. Ironbark Roofing's storm questions add the claim number and the adjuster's visit date. His request arrives with claim HX-40917 and a visit on November 12. Severin runs storm jobs and sees every storm request sorted by adjuster visit, soonest first.
fields.tab_content_3:
$1,960 for gutters, no price for the roof

Leyla Faraji wants new gutters and a new roof on her 2-story house. Gable Ridge Roofing prices gutters at $14 a foot. Her 140 feet show $1,960 before she submits. The roof replacement reads Priced after inspection. Her roof is 23 years old, and the request goes to Nadira, the estimator, to book a visit.
fields.tab_content_4:
After the inspection, Pernille signs for metal

Juniper Crest Roofing inspects Pernille Zubiri's roof and sends one quote with two options: architectural shingles at $14,800 or standing-seam metal at $21,400. She picks metal and signs on her phone. The request now reads Signed, and the job goes on Feodor's crew schedule.

fields.howto_title: How to Create a Roofing Quote Form
fields.howto_description: Seven steps to create a roofing quote form that sorts requests by job type and holds roof prices until the inspection.
fields.howto_step_1_title: 01 Sort last season's calls into job types
fields.howto_step_2_title: 02 Ask for what decides the visit
fields.howto_step_3_title: 03 Make photos part of every request
fields.howto_step_4_title: 04 List the work you price without a visit
fields.howto_step_1_des: Go back through last season's calls and group them: leak repairs, storm damage, full replacements, and gutter work. Each group becomes a choice at the top of the form with its own follow-up questions. Leave off any work your crews turn down.
fields.howto_step_2_des: Ask for the address, the roof material, its age, and the number of stories. Those answers tell your estimator how long the visit takes and which ladder goes on the truck. Leave square footage for the estimator to measure on site.
fields.howto_step_3_des: Add a photo step that asks for one shot of the whole roof from the street and close shots of any damage. On a leak, ask for the ceiling stain inside too. Look at them before the visit to decide which section to check first.
fields.howto_step_4_des: Write down each add-on you charge one set price for, like a ridge vent per unit or new downspouts per linear foot. Those can show a total on screen. Anything that depends on the decking under the shingles waits for someone to go up.
fields.howto_step_5_title: 05 Pick who hears about each job type
fields.howto_step_5_des: Send active leaks to whoever is on call, by email, with a backup for weekends. Storm jobs can go to the person who meets adjusters, and replacements to the estimator who books visits. Write each rule down before you open Emergent.
fields.howto_step_6_des: Put the job types, the questions, the fixed rates, and the routing rules into one prompt. Emergent builds the form and the database behind it, plus the screen your estimator uses to send quotes. Ask for changes in plain English later.
fields.howto_step_7_title: 07 Send a test request from your phone
fields.howto_step_7_des: Report a test leak from your phone with water coming in now. Check that the email reaches the on-call lead with the photos and that the request shows no price. Then send yourself a test quote and sign it to watch the status change.

faq_plan.q: What is a roofing quote form?
faq_plan.a: A roofing quote form is the online request a homeowner fills in to ask a roofer for a price. It asks what kind of job it is and where the house is, then covers the roof itself: material, age, number of stories, and photos. The roofer prices small jobs from those answers and books an inspection for the rest.

faq_plan.q: How do I create a roofing quote form?
faq_plan.a: List your job types and the questions each one needs, then decide which work gets a price on screen and which waits for an inspection. Name who receives each request. Put all of it in one prompt to Emergent's AI form builder, which builds the form along with a database that holds every request.

faq_plan.q: Should a roofing quote form show a price before the inspection?
faq_plan.a: Only for work you charge one set rate for, like new gutters at a price per foot. Hold repair and replacement prices until someone has seen the roof up close, and mark that work Priced after inspection so the homeowner knows a visit comes next.

faq_plan.q: How is a roofing quote form different from other home service quote forms?
faq_plan.a: It asks about work above the homeowner's head, like how many stories the house has and what the damage looks like in photos. A cleaning quote form can price a job from the room count. A roofing quote form leads to a visit first.

faq_plan.q: What photos should a roofing quote form ask the homeowner for?
faq_plan.a: Ask for a wide photo of the roof taken from the street, plus close-ups of missing shingles or bent flashing. For a leak, add the stain on the ceiling below it. Tell the homeowner to stay on the ground and shoot from the yard.

faq_plan.q: How should a roofing quote form handle a roof that is leaking right now?
faq_plan.a: Ask if water is dripping inside right now and treat a yes as urgent: send the address and photos to whoever is on call, and tell the homeowner on the confirmation screen when to expect a call. An app built with Emergent can escalate the alert to a backup person.

faq_plan.q: Can one roofing quote form cover repairs and full replacements?
faq_plan.a: Yes. Make the job type the first question and give each type its own follow-ups: a repair asks where the damage is, and a replacement asks how old the roof is and when they hope to start. For a remodel that goes past the roof, use a construction quote form instead.

faq_plan.q: What should a roofing quote form ask after hail or wind damage?
faq_plan.a: Ask for the storm date and whether hail or wind did the damage. Then ask if the homeowner has filed an insurance claim, and if so, collect the claim number along with the date the adjuster plans to visit. Forms built with Emergent have no response caps when a storm brings a rush of requests.

faq_plan.q: Where do roofing quote form requests go after the homeowner sends one?
faq_plan.a: Each request becomes a row in a table, with its photos attached, that you can sort by visit date. With Emergent, that data lives in a database you own, and the app can connect to any CRM or calendar that has an API.

faq_plan.q: Should a roofing quote form ask what roof material the homeowner wants?
faq_plan.a: Yes, ask for the material on the roof now and the one they want next, such as asphalt shingles or metal. The answer shapes the options your estimator prices after the visit. Price the materials themselves with suppliers through a separate rfq form.

intent.evidence: Searchers want a quote form a roofer can use. The page gives the field set (FAQ 1, step 2), photo guidance (FAQ 5), storm and leak branches and pricing policy ('Hold repair and replacement prices until someone has seen the roof up close').

specificity.evidence: Uses roofing vocabulary throughout: 'decking under the shingles', 'bent flashing', 'which ladder goes on the truck', adjuster visit dates, gutters by the foot.

openers.evidence: Every body opens on a full sentence: 'Pick a leak repair and the form asks for the room below the leak', 'Anton Dobrev finds a brown stain spreading across his kitchen ceiling at 9:40 p.m.'

craft.evidence: Varied sentence length and no tacked-on endings; FAQ 6 and FAQ 7 have long sentences (recorded as a note).

voice.evidence: 'A voicemail saying the roof leaks gives a crew nothing to plan with. Two photos and the roof's age tell them what to bring.' reads like an operator wrote it.

truth.evidence: Each Emergent claim maps to claims_used (prompt-build, database-owned, alerts incl. escalation, e-signature-capture, code-export, no-caps, api-connect). distinct.evidence: Has its own angle (roof prices held until inspection, active-leak alerts, storm claims with adjuster dates). Sibling forms are only linked: 'construction quote form', 'rfq form'.

faq.evidence: 10 on-topic questions, each answered in its first sentence, e.g. 'Only for work you charge one set rate for, like new gutters at a price per foot.' No brand or format asks.
